title: Time Bender
blurb: History's dates are messing with you. Three are real, one is cap. Trust nothing.

cards.say: [Harvard University is older than calculus], [the steam train is older than the bicycle], [Big Ben is older than the United States], and [Disneyland opened before Hawaii became a state].
cards.real: Big Ben's clock tower in London was finished in 1859, more than 80 years after the United States declared independence in 1776.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Trevithick's steam locomotive ran on rails in 1804; Karl Drais's running machine, the first bicycle, came in 1817 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Trevithick
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Big Ben's tower and Great Clock were finished in 1859; the US declared independence in 1776 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ben

cards.say: [Napoleon was still alive when the oldest surviving photo was taken], [Florence Nightingale lived long enough to have her voice recorded], [Queen Victoria lived long enough to be filmed on a movie camera], and [Harriet Tubman was still alive when the Wright brothers first flew].
cards.real: Napoleon died in 1821. The oldest surviving camera photo, a view from a window in France by Nicephore Niepce, dates from 1826 or 1827.

cards.say: [Pluto was discovered and demoted within one person's lifetime], [Uranus was discovered while the American Revolution was still going on], [Neptune finished its first full orbit since its discovery in 2011], and [the Moon landing is closer to the Wright brothers' first flight than to 2025].
cards.real: The Wright brothers flew in 1903 and Apollo 11 landed in 1969, 66 years apart. From 1969 to 2025 is only 56 years.

cards.say: [the authors C.S. Lewis and Aldous Huxley died on the same day], [the rivals Thomas Edison and Nikola Tesla died on the same day], [the composers Bach and Handel were born in the same year], and [Marilyn Monroe and Queen Elizabeth II were born in the same year].
cards.real: Thomas Edison died in 1931. His rival Nikola Tesla outlived him by more than 11 years and died in January 1943.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Edison died October 18, 1931; Tesla died January 7, 1943 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla

cards.say: [Notre-Dame in Paris is older than Machu Picchu], [the concrete dome of Rome's Pantheon has stood for about 1,900 years], [the Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure for over 3,700 years], and [the main pyramid at Chichen Itza is older than the Roman Colosseum].
cards.real: Rome's Colosseum opened in AD 80. El Castillo, the great pyramid at Chichen Itza, was built centuries later, sometime between the 700s and 1100s AD.

cards.say: [Pocahontas visited London while Shakespeare was still alive], [Moctezuma still ruled the Aztecs when Henry VIII became king], [the first traffic light was installed before Karl Benz built his first car], and [the Rosetta Stone was found after the U.S. Constitution was written].
cards.real: Shakespeare died in April 1616. Pocahontas didn't arrive in England until June 12 that year, about seven weeks later.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Moctezuma II ruled the Aztecs from 1502 to 1520; Henry VIII became king of England in April 1509 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moctezuma_II
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) the Rosetta Stone was found in July 1799; the US Constitution was written and signed in 1787 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone

cards.say: [President John Tyler was born in 1790 and had a grandson alive in 2024], [a veteran of the American Revolution was photographed in 1864], [a Civil War veteran was still alive when Apollo 11 landed on the Moon], and [a signer of the Declaration of Independence broke ground for a railroad in 1828].
cards.real: The last undisputed Civil War veteran, Albert Woolson, died in 1956, 13 years before Apollo 11.

cards.say: [the Ottoman Empire still existed when the first airplanes flew], [the Tour de France is older than the modern Olympic Games], [Coca-Cola was invented before the Eiffel Tower was built], and [Alaska still belonged to Russia when Abraham Lincoln died].
cards.real: The modern Olympics began in Athens in 1896. The first Tour de France was raced seven years later, in 1903.

cards.say: [women first competed at the Olympics in 1928], [golf came back to the Olympics in 2016 after 112 years away], [the Olympics handed out medals for painting until 1948], and [the first basketball game ever played ended 1 to 0].
cards.real: Women first competed at the 1900 Paris Olympics, in sports like tennis and golf. 1928 is when women's track and field was added.

cards.say: [the Soviet Union still existed when the first website went online], [Macau was still ruled by Portugal when Google was founded], [the first message sent over the early internet crashed it after two letters], and [the first email was sent after the first Apple computer went on sale].
cards.real: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971. Apple's first computer, the Apple I, didn't go on sale until 1976.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Google was founded in September 1998; Portugal handed Macau over to China on December 20, 1999 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_sovereignty_over_Macau

cards.say: [Star Wars came out closer to the end of World War II than to 2025], [Mount Rushmore was finished before Mickey Mouse first appeared], [World War I ended before American women won the right to vote nationwide], and [Abraham Lincoln's son was at the Lincoln Memorial's dedication in 1922].
cards.real: Mickey Mouse debuted in Steamboat Willie in 1928. Work on Mount Rushmore didn't stop until October 1941.

cards.say: [the last verified person born in the 1800s died in 2017], [Japan's last shogun was still alive when the first Model T was sold], [China's last emperor died before the first person went to space], and [the Holy Roman Empire still existed when the United States was founded].
cards.real: Puyi, China's last emperor, died in 1967, six years after Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space.
